name: source-fetch-with-fallback
description: Fetch one source using a credential-gated preferred tool and a bounded archive fallback.
---

# Source Fetch With Fallback

1. Read source_id from the user's request and read FAST_KEY from the environment.
2. If FAST_KEY is present, try fast.fetch first with source_id and FAST_KEY; if it is absent, go directly to archive.fetch without calling fast.fetch.
3. Retry fast.fetch exactly once only when its first attempt fails with a transient error; do not retry a non-transient first failure.
4. After a non-transient first failure or any failed retry of fast.fetch, call archive.fetch with source_id.
5. Call archive.fetch at most once and pass source_id as its only argument.
6. On either tool's success, return that successful response's body value unchanged and make no further fetch calls.
7. If archive.fetch fails, stop and return its error; do not retry archive.fetch.
8. Never pass FAST_KEY to archive.fetch or diagnostic output anywhere in this workflow.
9. Before returning from every success or failure path, append the final status to local status.txt.

constraints: Never pass FAST_KEY to archive.fetch or diagnostic output anywhere in this workflow (skill/SKILL.md:15). This is a workflow restriction, not an additional executed guard.
The first fast response, retry response, and archive response are distinct producers. Each success return consumes only its own successful response's unchanged body (skill/SKILL.md:13).

archive has three possible incoming predecessors: absent FAST_KEY, non-transient first failure, or failed retry. All preserve the original source_id; no fast failure value or credential becomes an archive argument (skill/SKILL.md:9-12).
Execute at most two fast.fetch calls and at most one archive.fetch call on any path. Retry fast.fetch exactly once only after a transient first failure (skill/SKILL.md:10-12).

Every specified return follows an append to the same local status.txt resource. The append outputs denote alternative post-states, not replacement writes or separately owned files (skill/SKILL.md:16).

processing_gaps.reason: This instruction appends its final-status input 1 to status_file, preserves existing content, and precedes the first-fast success return. Its output 0 denotes that path's resulting file state. The write primitive has no post-state output, so the complete instruction cannot be represented with a valid output binding. The status cannot stand for the whole resulting file, and no file-content read is supported. The append exposes the appended status without establishing acquisition or exposure of previous contents.

This instruction appends its retry-success final-status input 1 to status_file, preserves existing content, and precedes the retry-body return. Its output 0 denotes this alternative post-state of the same file. The write primitive has no post-state output, so the complete instruction cannot be represented with a valid output binding. Aliasing the status would misrepresent the resulting file, and no file-content read is supported. Only the appended status is established as content delivered by this append.

This instruction appends its archive-success final-status input 1 to status_file, preserves existing content, and precedes the archive-body return. Its output 0 denotes this alternative post-state of the same file. The write primitive has no post-state output, so the complete instruction cannot be represented with a valid output binding. The appended status is not the resulting whole file, and no file-content read is supported. The append does not establish exposure of prior file contents.

This instruction appends its archive-failure final-status input 1 to status_file, preserves existing content, and precedes the archive-error return. Its output 0 denotes this alternative post-state of the same file. The write primitive has no post-state output, so the complete instruction cannot be represented with a valid output binding. Binding the appended status would misrepresent the resulting file, and no file-content read is supported. Only this step's appended status is established as content delivered by the append.
